problem: What is the domain of the function $f(x)=\operatorname{tan}⁡(2x)?$  Assume that $n$ is an integer.
worked_solution:
The domain of $y=\operatorname{tan}⁡x$ is given by

$$
x\ne \frac{\pi }{2}+n\pi ,
$$

where $n$ is an integer.

To find the domain of $\operatorname{tan}⁡(2x),$ we replace the $x$ on the left-hand side of the above with $(2x).$ This gives

$$
2x\ne \frac{\pi }{2}+n\pi .
$$

Solving for $x,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}2x & \ne \frac{\pi }{2}+n\pi  \\ x & \ne \frac{\pi }{2\cdot 2}+\frac{n\pi }{2} \\ x & \ne \frac{\pi }{4}+\frac{n\pi }{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the domain of the function is $x\ne \frac{\pi }{4}+\frac{n\pi }{2},$ where $n$ is an integer.
